description: Drum pattern generator driven by a phasor rather than a clock, a port of Mutable Instruments Grids: a ramp sweeps 32 steps of a bar, and three channels of triggers and accents come off a map

params.text: Moves east and west across the map of drum patterns, blending the four patterns nearest the point chosen; in Euclid it sets the pattern length for channel 1 instead
Moves north and south across the map of drum patterns, blending the four patterns nearest the point chosen; in Euclid it sets the pattern length for channel 2 instead
Adds random variation to the pattern, drawn afresh each time the phasor returns to 0V; at the bottom of its travel the bar repeats exactly. In Euclid it sets the pattern length for channel 3 instead
Sets how many of that channel's steps fire, from none at the bottom of its travel to the densest the chosen pattern offers at the top
Selects the pattern source: Original and Henri are two maps of drum patterns, Euclid replaces them with a Euclidean rhythm on each channel

inputs.text: A ramp from 0V to 10V across one bar, cut into 32 steps by where the voltage is; running it backwards plays the bar backwards, and holding the voltage steady holds one step
Added to the Map X knob, 10V covering the knob's whole travel, and the total held within it
Added to the Map Y knob, 10V covering the knob's whole travel, and the total held within it
Added to the Chaos knob, 10V covering the knob's whole travel, and the total held within it
Added to that channel's Fill knob, 10V covering the knob's whole travel, and the total held within it
Added to the Mode knob at one mode per 2.5V, the total rounded and held within the three modes; it is read only while a cable is patched

outputs.text: A 1ms pulse at 10V on each step that channel fires; the Trigger Mode menu item turns it into a gate lasting half a step instead
A 1ms pulse at 10V on the steps that channel fires with an accent; in Euclid it fires where that channel's Euclidean pattern comes back round to its start instead

notes: a phasor drives this, not a clock: a ramp rising from 0V to 10V once per bar, from Phasor Generator, Clock to Phasor or an LFO's saw output. Nothing moves here until one is patched in.
in Euclid the patterns are read on every second step, so a bar holds 16 places rather than 32 and the odd-numbered steps are always silent.
the lamp above each channel's jacks lights for 100ms whenever that channel fires, whichever of the two output jacks the pulse went to.
every jack on the module is monophonic; only the first channel of a polyphonic cable is read, and each output carries one channel.
menu: Trigger Mode: Pulse, Gate — Pulse sends a 1ms pulse on each hit, Gate holds the output high for the first half of the step the hit falls on
